steps.name: Load, QC, and harmonize counts/metadata
steps.question: Do the 6 samples in metadata.csv (3 treated, 3 control) match the sample columns in counts.csv (12000 genes x 7 columns), and are there outlier samples or batch structure that would compromise the treated-vs-control comparison?
acceptance_criteria: Sample names in metadata.csv are confirmed to match column names in counts.csv 1:1 (accounting for the extra gene-symbol column)
Library size, gene detection rate, and a PCA or sample-to-sample correlation heatmap on variance-stabilized/log-CPM data are produced for all 6 samples
Any sample flagged as an outlier (e.g., >2 SD from group centroid on PC1/PC2) is reported explicitly, not silently dropped
Low-count genes (e.g., rows with near-zero counts across all samples) are flagged for filtering prior to DE testing

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: treated vs control
steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between the 3 treated and 3 control liver samples (Salmon raw gene counts), using DESeq2 with an unpaired two-group design?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 run with design ~condition on raw integer counts, condition releveled so control is the reference
Low-count genes filtered before testing (e.g., minimum count/CPM threshold across samples) and the filtering rule reported
Log2 fold changes shrunk with apeglm (or ashr as fallback) for stable effect-size estimates given n=3 per group
Results table reports baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, pvalue, and BH-adjusted padj for all tested genes, ranked by padj
A results table (CSV) and an MA plot / volcano plot are produced
The step explicitly reports the number of genes passing padj<0.05 and separately padj<0.1, and states that with n=3/group only genes with large, consistent effects are reliably detectable

steps.name: Power and confidence assessment at n=3 per group
steps.question: Given the estimated dispersion from this dataset and n=3 replicates per arm, what minimum effect size (fold change) is this DESeq2 analysis powered to detect at FDR 0.05, and how should confidence in the DE gene list be qualified?
acceptance_criteria: Gene-wise and common/trended dispersion estimates from the fitted DESeq2 model are extracted and summarized (median, IQR) across the expressed gene set

A post-hoc power approximation (e.g., using the fitted mean-dispersion trend to simulate or analytically estimate detectable log2FC at alpha=0.05 for n=3 vs n=3) is reported, stating the fold-change threshold at which power is approximately 80%

The report explicitly states that unpaired n=3 vs n=3 designs are underpowered for small/moderate effects and lists genes near the significance boundary (0.05<padj<0.2) as candidates that a larger cohort could resolve either way
No claim of statistical confidence is made beyond what the dispersion/power calculation supports

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of DE genes (WikiPathways human)
steps.question: Which WikiPathways-defined biological pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control liver samples?
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment (e.g., hypergeometric/ORA on padj<0.05 gene set, or GSEA-style pre-ranked on the full log2FC-ranked gene list) run against the human WikiPathways gene sets available in the reference store
If fewer than ~10 genes pass padj<0.05, the step falls back to a pre-ranked GSEA on the full DESeq2 stat/log2FC ranking rather than failing, and this fallback is reported explicitly
Gene symbols in the DESeq2 results are matched to WikiPathways HGNC symbols; unmatched genes are counted and reported
Output is a ranked table of enriched pathways with adjusted p-values and leading-edge/member genes, plus a bar or dot plot of the top pathways
If the WikiPathways human reference is unavailable at run time, the step reports this gap rather than silently skipping enrichment

plan.title: Liver DE: treated vs control (n=3/group)
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a bulk RNA-seq gene-level count matrix (12000 genes x 7 columns, 6 samples per metadata) from Salmon, human liver, 3 treated vs 3 control, unpaired, single batch. Note: counts.csv is described as 12000 x 7 (likely gene column + 6 samples) while metadata.csv is 6 x 2 (sample + condition) — consistent with 6 samples total, 3 per group. With n=3 per group, statistical power is inherently limited: DESeq2's negative-binomial model with empirical Bayes shrinkage of dispersion is the appropriate tool (it is designed for exactly this small-n regime), but the plan must be explicit that at n=3 the analysis can detect only large, consistent effects, dispersion estimates are highly uncertain, and any single-gene call should be interpreted with corresponding caution. The plan: (1) load and QC counts/metadata, harmonize sample identifiers, run PCA/sample correlation to check for outliers or mislabeling; (2) run DESeq2 differential expression treated-vs-control with standard filtering and independent filtering, apply apeglm shrinkage for stable fold-change estimates given small n, report FDR (BH) with explicit power caveats; (3) run functional enrichment (WikiPathways human gene sets, confirmed present) on the DE gene list to contextualize the transcriptional program affected; (4) produce a power/confidence assessment step quantifying what effect sizes are detectable at n=3 per group (e.g., via dispersion estimates and post-hoc power approximation) so the confidence question is answered quantitatively rather than asserted qualitatively.
